question: The major focus of my recent travels has been visiting all of the UNESCO World Heritage sites. When I visit a new country, I feel like it helps me appreciate where I am staying for more than just a few popular sites I have seen on social media. I have been paying special attention to what they call "The List in Danger," and I like to prioritize those locations if possible. I have recently visited Cameroon and Chad, and I think that my next destination will be the Democratic Republic of the Congo in June 2025. While I am there, it is my dream to see a Kordofan giraffe. Where could I see them when I visit?

answer:
**The only place in the Democratic Republic of Congo where you can see Kordofan giraffes is Garamba National Park.** | What you’ll need to know | Details | |--------------------------|---------| | **Location** | In the far‑northeastern corner of the DRC, in Haut‑Uélé Province, roughly 30 km east of the towns of Goma and Beni. The park covers about 4 900 km² of open savannah, woodland, and swamps. | | **UNESCO status** | Inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 1980; **listed on UNESCO’s “World Heritage List in Danger”** because of poaching, political instability and lack of funding. The park’s fragile ecosystem is protected by the World Heritage Committee. | | **Why it’s a Kordofan hotspot** | Garamba holds the last remaining, isolated population of the **Kordofan giraffe (Giraffa camelopardalis antiquorum)** – a critically‑endangered subspecies with fewer than 2,000 individuals worldwide. The park is the sole sanctuary for this giraffe in the DRC. | | **Best time to visit** | The dry season (June – September) is ideal: wildlife is easier to spot, roads are more passable, and the park’s 4‑night camping or lodge stays are more comfortable. | | **How to get there** | *Fly into Goma (or sometimes Kigali, Rwanda, then a domestic flight).
* From Goma, charter a small plane to the **Nagero airstrip** inside Garamba – this is the most common way to enter the park.
* Alternatively, a 2‑day overland “bush‑trail” trek from Goma is possible but more time‑consuming. | | **Tour operators and permits** | * **African Parks** manages the park and offers full safari packages. You’ll need a park permit (usually arranged through your tour operator).
* **Local guides** are mandatory in the park; they know the “giraffe circuit” and can direct you to the best viewing spots in the savannah zones. | | **What to expect** | • Small herds of about 40–60 giraffes wander the savannah. They’re also slimmer, paler, and have irregular lower‑leg patches – the classic Kordofan look.\n• Other flagship species include forest elephants, hippos, lions, and the iconic shoebill stork in the marshes.\n• Because of the park’s “in danger” status, conservation projects are active – you can meet rangers and see how anti‑poaching teams operate. | | **Practical tips** | • Pack light‑weight, neutral‑colored clothing – you’ll blend into the savannah.\n• Bring reef‑safe sunscreen, insect repellent, and a good camera (most giraffes are easier to photograph from a walking safari or short drive on foot).\n• Consider traveling in a small group (4–5 people) to reduce your impact and increase safety.\n• Stay overnight at a lodge or camp near the park’s boundary; this will give you early‑morning or late‑afternoon game drives when giraffes are most active. | ### Quick travel checklist (June 2025) | Item | Recommendation | |------|----------------| | **Visa** | DRC visa on arrival or e‑visa; require a valid passport. | | **Health** | Yellow fever vaccination (required for many travelers), malaria prophylaxis, routine vaccinations, travel insurance. | | **Money** | Swiss franc or US dollar accepted at airports; small change in local currency (CDF) for park fees. | | **Safety** | Check the latest travel advisories (some travel warning since 2020); avoid traveling alone in remote areas. | | **Cultural respect** | Learn a few basic DRC French phrases; be respectful of local customs and ask permission before photographing people. | --- #### Sources 1. **Garamba National Park – UNESCO World Heritage Site** – “Home: Garamba National Park…Kordofan Giraffe ‘last remaining population in the DRC’.” (https://giraffeconservation.org/programs/kordofan-giraffe-conservation-in-drc/) 2. **African Parks guide to Garamba** – “Garamba National Park in northeast DRC is home to critically endangered Kordofan giraffes.” (https://drctourism.com/garamba-national-park-kordofan-giraffe-safari) 3. **Wikipedia “Garamba National Park”** – description of location, area, UNESCO inscription. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park) > *“In June 2025, you’ll be able to see the last remaining Kordofan giraffes in the wild at Garamba National Park, a UNESCO Heritage site that’s on the ‘List in Danger.’ Plan a short charter flight from Goma to the park’s Nagero airstrip, schedule a guided giraffe safari, and you’ll witness one of the world’s most critically endangered giraffe subspecies in its natural environment.”*

## Where to See Kordofan Giraffes in DRC — Complete Safari Guide
Garamba National Park in northeast DRC is home to critically endangered Kordofan giraffes, forest elephants, hippos, and lions — one of Africa's oldest and most exclusive national parks, managed by African Parks with zero tourist crowds.
Quick Answer
**Yes, there are giraffes in the DRC.** Garamba National Park hosts Kordofan giraffes (Giraffa camelopardalis antiquorum) — one of the rarest giraffe subspecies. The park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site established in 1938, covering 4,902 km² in northeast DRC's Haut-Uélé Province.

## Kordofan Giraffes — Congo's Rarest Giants
The **Kordofan giraffe** (_Giraffa camelopardalis antiquorum_) is one of the most endangered giraffe subspecies in the world, with fewer than 2,000 individuals remaining in the wild. Garamba National Park in northeast DRC is one of its last strongholds.
Distinguished by their paler coloring and irregular patches that extend further down their legs compared to other subspecies, Kordofan giraffes were once widespread across Central and West Africa. Today, their range has collapsed dramatically.
African Parks, in partnership with ICCN (Congo's wildlife authority), has significantly improved the park's security and infrastructure since 2005, creating conditions for wildlife recovery and limited but growing tourism access.
Scientific Name Giraffa camelopardalis antiquorum
Conservation Status Critically Endangered (IUCN)
Wild Population< 2,000 individuals
Location in DRC Garamba National Park, Haut-Uélé
Distinguishing Feature Paler patches extending to lower legs

steps.text:
**The only place in the Democratic Republic of Congo where you can see Kordofan giraffes is Garamba National Park.** | What you’ll need to know | Details | |--------------------------|---------| | **Location** | In the far‑northeastern corner of the DRC, in Haut‑Uélé Province, roughly 30 km east of the towns of Goma and Beni. The park covers about 4 900 km² of open savannah, woodland, and swamps. | | **UNESCO status** | Inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 1980; **listed on UNESCO’s “World Heritage List in Danger”** because of poaching, political instability and lack of funding. The park’s fragile ecosystem is protected by the World Heritage Committee. | | **Why it’s a Kordofan hotspot** | Garamba holds the last remaining, isolated population of the **Kordofan giraffe (Giraffa camelopardalis antiquorum)** – a critically‑endangered subspecies with fewer than 2,000 individuals worldwide. The park is the sole sanctuary for this giraffe in the DRC. | | **Best time to visit** | The dry season (June – September) is ideal: wildlife is easier to spot, roads are more passable, and the park’s 4‑night camping or lodge stays are more comfortable. | | **How to get there** | *Fly into Goma (or sometimes Kigali, Rwanda, then a domestic flight).
* From Goma, charter a small plane to the **Nagero airstrip** inside Garamba – this is the most common way to enter the park.
* Alternatively, a 2‑day overland “bush‑trail” trek from Goma is possible but more time‑consuming. | | **Tour operators and permits** | * **African Parks** manages the park and offers full safari packages. You’ll need a park permit (usually arranged through your tour operator).
* **Local guides** are mandatory in the park; they know the “giraffe circuit” and can direct you to the best viewing spots in the savannah zones. | | **What to expect** | • Small herds of about 40–60 giraffes wander the savannah. They’re also slimmer, paler, and have irregular lower‑leg patches – the classic Kordofan look.\n• Other flagship species include forest elephants, hippos, lions, and the iconic shoebill stork in the marshes.\n• Because of the park’s “in danger” status, conservation projects are active – you can meet rangers and see how anti‑poaching teams operate. | | **Practical tips** | • Pack light‑weight, neutral‑colored clothing – you’ll blend into the savannah.\n• Bring reef‑safe sunscreen, insect repellent, and a good camera (most giraffes are easier to photograph from a walking safari or short drive on foot).\n• Consider traveling in a small group (4–5 people) to reduce your impact and increase safety.\n• Stay overnight at a lodge or camp near the park’s boundary; this will give you early‑morning or late‑afternoon game drives when giraffes are most active. | ### Quick travel checklist (June 2025) | Item | Recommendation | |------|----------------| | **Visa** | DRC visa on arrival or e‑visa; require a valid passport. | | **Health** | Yellow fever vaccination (required for many travelers), malaria prophylaxis, routine vaccinations, travel insurance. | | **Money** | Swiss franc or US dollar accepted at airports; small change in local currency (CDF) for park fees. | | **Safety** | Check the latest travel advisories (some travel warning since 2020); avoid traveling alone in remote areas. | | **Cultural respect** | Learn a few basic DRC French phrases; be respectful of local customs and ask permission before photographing people. | --- #### Sources 1. **Garamba National Park – UNESCO World Heritage Site** – “Home: Garamba National Park…Kordofan Giraffe ‘last remaining population in the DRC’.” (https://giraffeconservation.org/programs/kordofan-giraffe-conservation-in-drc/) 2. **African Parks guide to Garamba** – “Garamba National Park in northeast DRC is home to critically endangered Kordofan giraffes.” (https://drctourism.com/garamba-national-park-kordofan-giraffe-safari) 3. **Wikipedia “Garamba National Park”** – description of location, area, UNESCO inscription. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garamba_National_Park) > *“In June 2025, you’ll be able to see the last remaining Kordofan giraffes in the wild at Garamba National Park, a UNESCO Heritage site that’s on the ‘List in Danger.’ Plan a short charter flight from Goma to the park’s Nagero airstrip, schedule a guided giraffe safari, and you’ll witness one of the world’s most critically endangered giraffe subspecies in its natural environment.”*
